utterances.text: Fortunately it was the majority. The majority of the Serbs who supported me. And as for these two, whose names I gave you, I don't consider them to be great Serbs, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you also received assurances that the local police station, where Mr. Markocevic was, also wouldn't stand in your way, nor would they put themselves on the side of the Mice Group?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who could have caused trouble for us, we managed to win them over, to bring them over to our side. Had we not done that, there would have been ... I have no idea what would have been. May I add a sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that operation, the biggest problem arose when all of the soldiers from front lines, citizens of Teslic, and all civil population of Teslic wanted to join this operation. We didn't want to have the front lines emptied from soldiers, and we knew that the more people participated, the greater there were chances for casualties. That was an assessment I made as a reserve officer from the Bileca school, and I was top of my year while I was at that school, just so you know. Therefore, I wanted to have a operation that would involve as few people as possible from the ratio was 1:3. In areas where there were ten of them, we would send 30 of ours. And so on. As for the rest who wanted to participate, we put them in reserve forces. We made sure they were not in the front. It may look comical to you now, but in just one location, in the Kardijal Hotel, at the Vrucica Banja, we found 1200 casings from machine-gun bullets that had been fired at us when we surrounded them at the hotel. You can just imagine there were perhaps some 20 of them there, just so you don't think that all they had was slingshots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, it's time for the break, so if we could -- if this is a convenient point. Before we rise, the -- we received a motion from the Office of the Prosecutor on the 27th of May in relation to a witness who is scheduled to attend within the next three weeks. It -- the -- the application for that witness would be heard by videolink. It appears to be a matter without controversy, and we are inviting an expedited response from the Defence. 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The document that had been previously marked for identification, Mr. Olmsted, I take it you've seen the English translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Of 2D85. 1D03-3395, Exhibit 2D85.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, we have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And you have no reservations about the application to exhibit it, having read it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought it was a rhetorical question, but apparently it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I just have -- too many numbers that I can't remember the document. But I have been reminded of it, and we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we lift the MFI marking on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since we finally have the translation of this document, the document we discussed, let me show you briefly 1D -- 2D85; I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D85.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's the document you already saw. It has the description of a number of persons. All right. We have the English version now too. It says that the persons listed below have weapons which were made available to protect the interests, and names of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We made a digression, but let us go back to Teslic now and the answers you provided to us. You said that you managed to ensure the unity and consent of all relevant authorities in Teslic municipality, civilian and military, and you had the consent of the corps and a direct order from the Banja Luka CSB to carry out that operation, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I am wondering if there is any urgent need to elicit yet more information on the Mice operation. I think it has been cleared and -- and we've heard a lot of it so far. So unless you are able to convince me that there is a compelling need to proceed into this question, I suggest that you move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, I just need a few more pieces of information, not really details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And to conclude, so had you not been able to ensure this kind of a support at the local level from the Crisis Staff, military authorities, and so on, and the judiciary, this operation of yours -- it is not certain how it would have been carried out, and it could have produced many casualties, and its outcome could have been uncertain?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right. First of all, I could not have embarked upon that operation had there not been an order, had not the Banja Luka CSB stood firmly behind it. As for everything else, all the additional support, that was the prerequisite for us getting involved in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You must know that in certain municipalities in the territory under the jurisdiction of the CSB, certain Crisis Staffs and certain SJBs were absolutely beyond the control of the CSB due to political reasons?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the right reason, and I can enumerate additional -- or, rather, I can enumerate some examples. The most prominent one being Prijedor and Simo Drljaca, which represented a strong-hold that neither the Banja Luka CSB nor the entire republic, as far as I know, could do anything about. Why do I say "as far as I know"? Because, at the time, we tried first via military security and then later on via the Tajfun to insist on the removal the Simo Drljaca. Don't ask me how we wanted to move him, but we wanted to move him. And our request was not granted. They had no understanding for our request. Everybody kept saying that he had a support of local political organs so that any operation along the lines of the one carried out in Teslic could have resulted in serious bloodshed. And its outcome would have been completely uncertain, bearing in mind that, at the time, Simo Drljaca had full support of the entire army and police in that area. Also, do not underestimate the fact that the strongest military units in Republika Srpska came from that area. I don't know whether you need additional information. I can certainly tell you that. There were some other SJBs that were also prominent in this sense. The Prnjavor station tried to act in a similar way, as did Kotor Varos station for a while. But there were certainly very strong pressures at the local level exerted so that it wasn't possible to communicate with people in a civilised manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And to follow up, for the sake of transcript, when you said that Simo Drljaca had support of the army and police in that area, you were referring to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was referring to the local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when this operation was completed and when the criminal reports were filed and these people arrested and turned over to authorities, to your surprise, if I may say so, two or three days later, some of these people were released, Slobodan Karagic and some of his men, and this was done on the basis of an order from the basic court in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And before that, had you threats coming from that group.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But let me explain how come he and his group were released first. He came just one day before the operation, and this fact was established. Since it was also established who had killed one of our men at the Kardijal Hotel, we knew exactly who killed him and how, then it was a position of both the prosecution and the court, and I also acquiesced in that, that there was no evidence whatsoever that some of these people had committed a serious crime that would justify pre-trial detention. So everybody who had arrived Teslic on the eve of the operation was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this man, Karagic, actually sued you after the war, but if I understood the list that you showed us --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three cases in court against me in Teslic. One pursuant to an indictment submitted by the district prosecutor. He -- his name was Djuric. And then when he actually annulled the crime -- the criminal report submitted against me by the CSB in Doboj, this was followed by a private suit initiated by Slobodan Karagic and Stojan Djuric. These proceedings were also completed or ended, and the court, pursuant to the criminal report submitted by Slobodan Karagic, decided not to conduct the proceedings, or, in other words, it remained unresolved. And as for Stojan Djuric, prior to his death, and he fell seriously ill - he had cancer - so prior to his death, he actually revoked his criminal report against me before a court -- or in court, and he addressed the court on that occasion, apologising to me, to me personally. I accepted his apology because I knew -- I knew that the outcome of his disease was very predictable and that he only had days to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, if I may be of assistance. Page 56, line 17, it's a private criminal complaint. "Privatni crimnial tuzba" in Serbian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As for the rest of the group --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see document 1D03-1381.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tab number 19.

utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In Zupljanin register. [Interpretation] 1081; my apologies. In other words, 2D03-1081. There seems to be a problem with this document, so I will move on to something else. Perhaps we can have the document placed on the ELMO. Oh, all right, now we have it. No, I'm sorry, that's not the right document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It seems to be the one that you asked for Mr. Krgovic, isn't it? 21st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it is the 22nd of July, but I can't -- the 21st of July --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I can't see it here on our screens. 2D03-1081.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can I put on the ELMO the B/C/S version and the participant can follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No English. It was ... It was English, but it's disappeared somehow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, that's it. It's English version. So can I put the B/C/S version on the ELMO for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that it is on Sanction right now. Yeah, okay, there you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please take a look at this document. This is a ruling of the lower court in Teslic, dated the 21st of July, 1992, whereby detention of a large number of members of the Mice Group is cancelled. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the second page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This was signed by investigating judge Nenad Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, he was the president of the lower court in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the second paragraph, reading: "The investigating judge, in his letter number 1492/92 of 20 July 1992, the public prosecutor of Teslic agreed to release from custody individuals named in the disposition herein."

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The prosecutor was?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Branko Peric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the information that you had, that they were released from custody?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But only for the group that was released from custody before they were all released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will show you the other documents as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But could we now go back to page 1 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You can see here on the right-hand side it says: "At 1000 hours" and that -- or "at 1510," and then this is a sort of para -- signature or some initials. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This would suggest that this was received somewhere?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you another document related to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P1313, a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a log-book of the -- from the detention unit in Doboj, the custody log-book. I will now you show you the page indicated ERN 155935.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, 0415-5935. I believe it's page 21 in e-court. I think it's the next page; I apologise. 22. The next page. We should have on the screens number 143. In the left-hand column, 143. Page 5935, the last digits of the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So let's take a look at the first column. Let's see which individuals this relates to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The second part of this page, please, the left portion, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, it's the left-hand page of this log-book, not of this page, because the page is of a larger format. We only see the right-hand side of that page. Now could we see the left-hand side of that same page. So I would like to see the first half of this page marked in e-court as -- maybe -- it could be 5934. Maybe you can try that number. I apologise for the this, but, yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take look. Can you see the names here. So we have under number 143, Pijunovic Miroslav. And then we have Slobodan Tekic, Dobrivoje Culibrk, Stojan Djuric, Slavko Spasovic; all of these men are mens of the Mice Group?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So we see the last two names are Sljivic and Sljuka?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: They were released from custody in Teslic; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back to the page we had before, 5935.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now you can see that according to this log-book where it says "date of release," they were released on the 24th of July, 1992, at 1510. That is the same time that we saw where the ruling was received at the district court in Doboj. Can you see it in the third column, the last box at the bottom, the last two?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The 24th of July, 1992, at 1510.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And they were released pursuant to the Teslic lower court ruling, K 35/92. That's what we saw -- that's the document we saw a moment earlier?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to show the connection between this ruling, that note, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I think we've been there before, haven't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we haven't, Your Honour. Namely, one of our witnesses mentioned that these people were released from detention, and that's why I'm showing this. That they were released before the document reached the county prison in Doboj. And what I'm trying to show is what we can see in the upper right corner of this document, and we can also see it's the same handwriting as the one we found in the book. That was the purpose why I wanted to show this document to the witness, to present the entire release procedure. But we'll move to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, after you submitted a criminal report, after the persons were handed over to the investigative judge, the proceeding went on according to the law from that point on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And all the further activities, investigation, and everything else was under their jurisdiction. Am I right in saying that? All the investigative activities were, according to the law, under their authority?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it was before, and that's how it is still today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You are probably familiar with the fact that part of this process, there is one investigative step, namely, it was necessary to obtain forensic evidence as well and that the relevant organs issued an order to that effect?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of all that. I don't know how to explain it differently. That was under their jurisdiction. You do know that the Ministry of Interior, according to the law, cannot order exhumations, cannot order any forensic expertise. Even if they have an expert, forensic expert, among their ranks, they cannot launch into such an expertise without receiving an order from either a investigative judge or the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when you addressed Mr. Zupljanin in relation to the investigative steps that are under the jurisdiction of the prosecutor, was for the purpose of him to try and maybe speed up the process through his influence, to use his clout to ask the judicial organs to provide the necessary resources?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Let me explain why we needed -- why we asked for the process to be speeded up. We had two locations, two mass graves. In one grave, there was 20; in the other, 28 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You told us about it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that's why we asked for it. Namely, we didn't want something to happen, something that had occurred on other -- in other cases earlier, namely, that remains should be removed. We wanted to have this exhumation and a post-mortem to be conducted, knowing that the remains of persons killed -- for them to be something that can be recognised by their closest relatives but also to almost everything in Teslic because Teslic is a small town and people know each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But unrelated to this, after prosecutor had suggested, the investigative judge actually started the process which then took its stride?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you do remember that at the same time, simultaneously, a proper avalanche of accusations came that you did not abide by the procedure that was reported by the CSB Doboj; there were some privately-filed complaints by individuals involved. It all came immediately after. Do you remember those events?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do remember. Sorry to say that. It's a notorious fact. I gave my statement before the relevant organs in Teslic, before the court in Teslic, and I saw there that they have this in their records. In other words, for me to reiterate that would be a waste of time, of your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean it like that. I wanted to lay the foundation for my next question. When you discussed with Mr. Zupljanin this issue, when he told you, Radule, don't you get involved with that. Let the court deal with it. You have enough problems as it is. That was the essence of what he was trying to tell you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember now, and let me repeat this: I did not have frequent conversations with Stojan Zupljanin; I can only remember the events about which we talked. I told that to the Prosecutor, and I'm telling you this again. I did not have direct contact about various information with Stojan Zupljanin. And in relation to my conversation with Stojan in Teslic, I believe that this was a conversation that was by the book, a conversation between a superior and subordinate officer. My arrival at SUP on the next day, at 9.00 a.m., showed me that he was very much interested in making sure that the persons who perpetrated the crimes were arrested and charges brought against them. His first question was how many people were killed. I thought he had asked me about my group. And when I responded by saying one was killed among them and one among us, I remember Mr. Stevilovic then saying, Congratulations; that's fine. Because, as a soldier, his assessment before the start of the operation was that there will be a lot of casualties among us and that we have to be prepared for that. The view was, so to speak, that only children should not be sent into this operation, namely, people who don't have brothers, for instance, or siblings. And also not to send those who have small children, because we assumed that there would be many more casualties. To be fully honest, what we had in mind was casualties among our ranks. Nobody was thinking about how many casualties would there be among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And Stojan Zupljanin and Stevilovic congratulated you on the success of the operation? That's what they said?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood them. Lest I forget, one of the reasons why I left Teslic rather soon was because of a suggestion that came from Belgrade as well, saying, You should not be dealing with public security service issues; you are educated to be a state security personnel and to collect intelligence. They already had information that somebody is getting ready to kill me and that the person closest to the preparations for my killing were people by the name of Predrag Rakocevic [phoen] and Marinko Dukic. It was only 1998 that I had an opportunity to have a discussion with them openly about all the aspects of the events past, and I still remember Marinko Dukic telling me from a man I hated most to -- during the period between 1992 and today, I realised that same man was my best friend. I remember that well. And Marinko Dukic is a very straightforward person. Predrag Markocevic [phoen] said the same thing. And at about that time I managed to clear up matters also with Andrija Bjelosevic in relation to all the events that were unclear to him. So one cannot say that all the traces we left behind were bad. After a while, through conversation, clarification of issues, we would come to a conclusion that a huge number of people who had initially seen us as enemies, traitors, and so forth, finally accepted us as professionals, human beings, and true members of our nation. I apologise for this discourse which was rather long, but that's how things were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Following this, you handed over the public security station to the people who were appointed, and then you left the area and re-joined the State Security Service, continued your work as a part of the Milos Group?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There was a misunderstanding that occurred a bit earlier, and I would like to ask you to clarify this for me. We were talking about -- about the Milos Group members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we move to the private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I think it may have been the day before yesterday in responding to the questions by the Prosecutor who showed you a document concerning a unit from Teslic that was part of the VRS which was not within the hierarchy. We asked -- you asked for them to be -- to join the public security station in order to put them under control and help this public security station in their fight against self-proclaimed groups and para-formations and their criminal activities. Mainly because this group was an experienced group of fighters. According to you, they could have been incorporated with -- into the police force, and you believed they would be a positive force in resolving more complex problems?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It was a smaller company headed by Lieutenant Jocic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The idea was to put them under control because the risk was that they might become a paramilitary formation on their own and become a security problem?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They took part in the arrest of the Mices. Up until that point, there was no reason to treat them as perpetrators of crimes of any sort, especially not of war crimes. And I believe that a high-quality unit like that with good training should be signed on because my intention was, in the capacity of the chief of the public security station, to make sure that we, the public security station, will take care of another two or three groups, primarily a group of rebels from Blatnica, who were also committing crimes at the time, as well as with a certain Bubic, from the area of the village of Pribinic, who, for a while, was some kind of a warden or commander of some detention unit, unorganised detention unit. I don't know whose interests he was working for, but we prevented him from continuing with his activities. There were also other smaller groups present in Teslic, again, involved in committing crimes against non-Serb population, and we had plans of taking care of that, making them -- putting them under control. We prepared reports about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We have seen the reports. We'll -- instead of going deeper into that, let me show you a document. The Prosecutor showed you a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, excuse me. Before we leave this issue, I was -- I was interested in exploring a bit Mr. Radulovic's comment that the Mice weren't really arrested for reasons of war crimes but, rather, for the commission of civilian crimes. Mr. Radulovic, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you didn't, and I apologise -- I regret that. They were, first of all, arrested because they had killed a number of persons of non-Serb ethnicity. That was the main reason why they were arrested and why a criminal report was filed. As for other things they did, everything was documented so that their ordinary, if I may say so, crime activity was in the background at the time. It wasn't given the priority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, another report of the Milos Group shown to you by Prosecutor concerns the establishment of the special police detachment. I'll show you the decision of the Assembly of -- of the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina. So could you now please be shown --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But before I put this to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreters ask you to repeat the number of the document, if you would be good enough. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Your document list, Mr. Krgovic, tab number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Tab 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Within the Milos Group, you did not really focus on the special detachment. It wasn't a particular focus of your attention. It's only if you came across some information on their activities. And you informed about them, in general terms, if it was of security interest for that region, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And please look at the second page of this document. The Assembly of Krajina established this detachment. And in the document it says that the detachment will comprise members of active and reserve police force. And then if you go to the next page then we will see what the intention of the Assembly was at the time. And you know how sometimes very good intentions produce evil results. It says here that the unit would be established in order to protect law and order, especially to protect against sabotage activities and so on. And then in paragraph 4 from the top it says how the detachment would be manned. And we can see in this paragraph that, first of all, there would be some active policemen in it who were skilled and who were part of the "posebni" detachment, which existed before the war. And then that out of the candidates that were available they should select those who had already been in similar units in Zagreb and Sarajevo and who had fled from the area as well as persons who already had some experience on the front line. It says here that some candidates have the relevant skills and expertise which would allow them to execute successfully any tasks and that those who were in reserve forces would remain in reserve forces until certain conditions were met, following which they would be transferred into active-force members. I apologise for speeding. So what is important? It's that certain persons who had front-line experience became members of the unit, and, unfortunately, some persons who really did not belong in that units and who did not meet the requirements also became members, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And, unfortunately, those who had no place in that unit had the main role.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honours. I have a problem with LiveNote, so I would kindly ask the assistance of technical unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when speaking of this, you said, Yes, there were such instances, and there were some honourable compensations and, yes, there were members who discharged their duties in a honourable and honest way.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence in-chief, you said that after these events, speaking of Stojan Zupljanin, you said that you had told him, in general terms, about the behaviour of members of that unit - this is page 10804 - when you came back from Doboj. And you received information, and you mention some colleagues of yours. And then in speaking of this event, you said that it wasn't really your job to wok on crime investigations. You said that there were some irregularities in the conduct of the members of that unit, saying that cars had been stolen and there was some unlawful activities related to detention and bringing in of persons, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation to finish. Mr. Krgovic, as far as I remember -- or to the extent that I remember events which took place 17 years ago, there's no reason why I shouldn't remember what I said four days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were in Doboj, you said that you didn't know what the circumstances were while they were there, who had sent them there, and how -- how they worked.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I conveyed this information, in general terms, to Stojan Zupljanin primarily in order to protect the members of our special detachment from the frequent occasions where they were used to shield local criminals. Everything that local criminals had done was mostly attributed to the members of the special detachment of police from Banja Luka and also partially was also attributed to members of the Red Berets unit. After saying this to Stojan Zupljanin, I proposed that they be withdrawn, and I said explicitly that, based on what I knew, it wasn't done the next day by the day after; namely, members of the special detachment were withdrawn from Doboj to Banja Luka, and they took several days in pulling out because they carried with them the items that they had seized or had stolen from shops, private enterprises, and so on. I saw with my own eyes. I concluded that Mr. Zupljanin accepted that information with due seriousness, giving it serious attention. I don't know whether he verified this with somebody or not, but the information about their withdrawal was provided to him by the Milos Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see OTP 65 ter 10355, please. 65 ter 10355.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a list, a payroll list, from Doboj, from the Doboj CSB, their police station. Here we can see that these people were on the payroll in Doboj. It is entitled: "The 9th Company for Special Assignments, Banja Luka." And then can you see the list of persons who were members. This is payroll for May. This is a much longer document, and I have shown only the first page. This is the page that I'm interested in. And based on what we can see here, they, as a unit, were detached to the Doboj CSB at the time. They received their salaries there. And they were issued assignments an orders there. It stems from this document, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be my conclusion too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And these are the people that you have mentioned as being there at the time?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I also mentioned other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted. Mr. Olmsted. For one thing, we don't have an English translation of this. But ... and I guess, apparently, it's so illegible that we can't get an English translation of it. So that's the only problem with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we could MFI it at this point. This document was on the OTP list in relation to the witness from Doboj who spoke of the same events, and I was sure there was a translation. Could we perhaps MFI it for the time being until we get a better copy, and then I'll give it to the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Brief question: How does this payroll list assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a payroll list from Doboj for the members of the special unit from Banja Luka, which, at the time, was deployed in Doboj and was under the jurisdiction of the Doboj authorities, the CSB and SJB in Doboj. This is why we want this to be tendered into evidence. It bears the stamp of the Doboj Crisis Staff, I think. This is where that unit was active in that capacity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But the assignment of such persons is independent of the specifics of the names on the list, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I will get to that. My question will also relate to other members. But when it comes to this company that the previous witness spoke about, he was from the police station in Doboj, there was some talk about payroll, et cetera. And the Prosecutor did not tender that document into evidence at the time. I guess it didn't suit them. So this is why I want it to be admitted now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think I understand your concerns. I don't see -- this document -- it's unclear who the special unit was. It's not clear from the witness's answer whether this is the Banja Luka Special Police Detachment or some other special unit that was created within Doboj. And, therefore, there is a bit of confusion as to its relevance to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may reply. It says clearly here: "The 9th Company for Special Tasks, Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you will agree with me, won't you, that this refers to that special unit from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, no offence - and this pertains to the Prosecutor as well - I know that this document pertains to the members of the special detachment from Banja Luka who had been deployed to Doboj. There's no doubt there whatsoever. I know that this is how they refunded salaries for those who had left their original unit and went to the area of another unit. I recognise some names here. And based on that, I can conclude that they were in the special police detachment from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I'm a bit at a loss as to what it is you wish to show to the Chamber about these members of the Banja Luka special detachment that were apparently replaced and sent to Doboj. What is the Chamber to make of this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the position of the Defence is - and we're trying to prove this on the basis of this document - is that the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the Ministry of Defence made a decision to resubordinate one company from the Banja Luka area and to redeploy them to Doboj where they acted under the command of the authorities of that town in order to defend the town. So they were there, they were active there, their salaries were paid out to them there, and they were granted all the rights that they were entitled to in Doboj. And this is what I'm trying to show. I'm trying to show the link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, this -- this is more or less clear. Why don't you just ask that question to the witness? Or is he not supposed to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has already answered my question. He said that they were deployed there and that they were under their command. But we can go over it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what you know and based on how they were redeployed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we must take the adjournment for the day. So, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can I just make my point quickly on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I mean, it's just still very unclear how this witness is coming to the conclusion that these are members of the Banja Luka Special Police Detachment. It's a very difficult document to read. At the very least, he should provide the names on this list who he leave believes were part of the Banja Luka Special Police Detachment. Otherwise, there's really no need to even go any further with this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will continue dealing with this, and I will also show to the witness a larger document, the list of the members of the special unit. And when you compare the names there with the names that the witness says he recognised, the conclusion will be clear to you. The document itself says that it is about the members of the 9th Company from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say something, I have glasses, but the names are legible, although hard to read, but still legible. And I recognise the names, first and last names, of the people whom I knew before the war and concerning whom I knew that during the war they were members of the special detachment. I told you everything now. There is no need for me to read this any further. I don't know all of these young men. That's true, I don't know all of them. But I saw two or three names on this list, and right now I can't tell you that I saw these persons in Doboj. But if it says on the top that this is a payroll, then I don't see why I shouldn't believe that these were members of our special detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Anyway, we'll pick up on this tomorrow morning. In the meantime, we'll marked for identification, so we don't lose it in the ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D89, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 1st day of June, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
